newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called lower extending consolidation.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called lower extending consolidation.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called lower Tuesday extending a consolidation that has lasted for three sessions amid scarce fundamental news.
"I think we are basically looking to test areas nearer to $19.00, extending this $19.50 to $20.50 range we have been in," said a New York crude trader.

Crude was called five to ten cents a barrel lower. Refined products were called flat to 0.25 cent a gallon lower. Dealers said it is possible that prompt crude will test and fall slightly below the double bottom on the daily spot continuation chart of $18.96 made early April.
Other dealers noted June crude has maintained a trendline extending from April 10 through April 17 on the spot chart, and could hold it again, with support seen between $19.50 and $19.60.
Still, rising crude supply continues to weigh on the market.
Independent assessments of OPEC production estimate that the organisation is producing close to 27 million barrels per day (bpd), above its agreed supply ceiling of 25.03 million bpd.
OPEC's ministerial output monitoring committee will meet in the Iranian city of Isfahan on May 7 to discuss the 11-member group's quota compliance, OPEC delegate sources in Iran said on Tuesday.
On the other side of the Atlantic, Brent futures on London's IPE were catching up to Monday's losses in NYMEX crude after the IPE was closed for a U.K. holiday.
On Monday, June crude ended three cents higher at $19.63 a barrel. June gasoline ended 0.02 cent up at 60.54 cents a gallon while June heating oil ended 0.03 cent a gallon higher at 53.05 cents.
